findings.title: A deeply nested JSON body now gets a 500, on /api/commands and, unsigned-in, on every /api/auth POST
findings.detail: Finding 34's fix moved the NUL check onto the parsed body, and `hasNul` walks it recursively. A body nested a few thousand levels deep overflows the stack (`RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`) and becomes a 500. Run 2 had this body as a 400. Under `/api/auth/*` it needs no session, so anyone can produce 500s and stack traces in the logs at will. Walk the value with an explicit stack, or cap the depth and answer 400.
findings.repro:
curl -X POST :8795/api/auth/email-otp/send-verification-otp -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @<(python3 -c "print('['*100000 + ']'*100000)")
curl -b ben.jar :8795/api/commands -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @<(python3 -c "print('['*5000 + ']'*5000)")

findings.title: Run 3: A code sent just before a suspension still signs in
Better Auth's own routes take `Origin: null`, and the send route takes `text/plain`
findings.detail: Sen's guard refuses a `null` Origin (finding 33), but Better Auth's routes accept one: sign-in by code and sign-out both answered 200 with `Origin: null`. The send route, now Sen's, reads any content type. The `SameSite=Lax` cookie keeps a cross-site page from using either, and signing in needs the code. Noted for consistency.
